title: an-emission-is-one-file-named-by-its-pointer
intention: A diagnostic emission is ONE FILE, named so its identity is readable without opening it — and the pointer becomes thin enough to be part of that name. TWO HALVES, ONE GRAIN. (1) THE SHAPE: cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py stops appending lines to a single per-instance diagnostics.jsonl and writes one JSON object per emission, at a name carrying the UTC-normalised microsecond stamp, the source device, and the crossing — Akien's `timestamp.inference.task.json`, shape ruled, spelling his. The reader contract does not move: BreadcrumbLog.records() still returns the trail in write order, so cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/inspector.py composes over it unchanged, which is the evidence that the grain moved and the contract did not. (2) THE POINTER: cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py passes `pointer=canonical` at all three of its emit sites — the whole canonicalised request, median 1,171 chars and max 10,078 — and passes a canonical DIGEST instead, the full text staying where it always was, in the inference_calls row's own canonical column. THE JOIN THAT MAKES THESE ONE NODE AND NOT TWO: the filename carries the task, so the file cannot be named until the pointer is short enough to BE a name. A 10,078-character pointer is not a filename on any filesystem here.
why: AKIEN, 2026-08-19, verbatim: 'logging emissions are supposed to be single json emissions. why are we adding rows to diagnostics.json?' — then, correcting his own framing in the next breath: 'i was expecting to see timestamp.inference.task.json or some such. and i have to be clear, i just created a contradiction. and just noticed it. each call is one task ticket recieving multiple emissions... but for a single inference call.' THE CONTRADICTION HE FLAGGED WAS MEASURED AND DISSOLVES, which is why this ticket is a grain change and not a redesign: across 140 emissions and 68 distinct pointers the gate sequences are only ever miss->hit (66 pointers) or miss->hit->hit->hit (2), and the gaps between two emissions sharing a pointer run min 3.2s, MEDIAN 282s, max 4,348s, with ZERO under one second. Those are separate calls minutes apart asking the same question, not one call emitting repeatedly. One inference call = exactly one emission, always. What made it read as 1:N is that the pointer is the PROMPT rather than the call — it names the question, and a question outlives the calls that ask it — which is the same fact the second half of this ticket fixes. AND HIS OWN STATED WHY IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CHANGE: the reason he gave for the one logs root on 2026-08-18 was retention, 'easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go'. A single appended trail CANNOT expire a record — mtime belongs to the file, so the sweep takes a device's whole history or none of it — while a file per emission gives per-record expiry for nothing. breadcrumb_log.py's own 'WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT' paragraph deferred rotation and evaporation on build-minimal grounds, correctly as a policy, and in doing so filed away the fact that the chosen grain could not express that policy when it arrived.

falsifier.proves_red: FALSIFIER — DONE when all five hold, and each is read off disk rather than off a return value. (1) ONE EMISSION IS ONE FILE: a real inference call (not a fixture) leaves exactly ONE new file under ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/, that file parses whole as a single JSON object, and no diagnostics.jsonl anywhere gains a line in the same window — measured by a before/after directory listing, never by asking the object what it wrote. (2) PER-RECORD EXPIRY IS REAL, which is the property the single trail CANNOT have and therefore the clause that makes this ticket worth its cost: stamp two emission files' mtimes at 31 and 1 days back, run one `find <logs root> -type f -mtime +30 -delete` against the ONE root, and exactly the old one is gone while the young one stands. Under today's shape that same command either deletes a device's entire history or nothing, and the proof must assert BOTH halves so the green is about expiry and not about deletion. (3) THE POINTER IS THIN AND STILL JOINS: inference_domain's emitted pointer falls inside the corpus band measured 2026-08-19 (every other trail's pointer median is 9-70 chars; inference_domain's is 1,171 with a max of 10,078 and accounts for 85% of that trail's 273,421 bytes), AND a record's pointer resolves to its inference_calls row by hashing that row's canonical column — proved against REAL rows already standing in the store, not against rows the proof wrote, because a join proved on self-written rows proves the hash function and not the join. (4) THE READER CONTRACT SURVIVES: BreadcrumbLog.records() returns the same records in the same write-order over the new shape, and cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/inspector.py reads them with no change to its own logic — the strongest available evidence that the grain moved and the contract did not. (5) THE AGREEMENT TOOTH STILL BITES: the count of gate='miss' emissions equals the count of verdict='miss' rows in inference_calls over the same window, matched by canonical DIGEST rather than canonical text — the substance of the sibling ticket's clause (c), preserved through the vocabulary change rather than quietly dropped by it. WRONG INTENT IF, and both directions are named because the grain can fail either way: reading one device's trail now costs a directory walk measurably slower than the single-file read it replaced at 30 days of records (the measure: time `records()` over a 5,600-file tree against the same records as lines — if the reader got worse, the picture got worse, and that is the parent's own 'logging happened, the picture did not' failure wearing this ticket's face); OR the digest makes a record unjoinable in practice — a pointer nobody can resolve back to its question is worse than a fat one, because a fat pointer is merely expensive and an unresolvable one is a record of truth that has stopped being a record. HORIZON: the next real inference call plus the first time a mind opens a trail to diagnose a red — needs no clock and no new instrument, because inference_domain is the sole path to every host so any real traffic tests clause (1), and clauses (2) and (3) are testable the moment the writer lands.

how: ONE writer, ONE reader contract, THREE call sites, and a blast radius counted before the build rather than discovered inside it. WRITER: cairn/tools/base/breadcrumb_log.py — RECORD_NAME and receive_diagnostic's open(..., 'a') become a per-record path; records() sorts the directory instead of splitting lines, and must tolerate BOTH shapes for one retention window because the 1,295 standing records are not migrated (cache-class; they age out where they lie). The stamp in the filename is NOT the record's `ts` verbatim: `ts` is an ISO string carrying an offset and does not sort lexically as time does across offsets, so the name carries a UTC-normalised YYYYMMDD.HHMMSS.uuuuuu — the shape the launcher's boot log already uses, borrowed as a pattern and cited, not grafted. POINTER: domain.py:319, :373, :408 pass a digest of `canonical`; the store keeps the text (domain.py:91, `canonical text NOT NULL`), so any reader joins by re-hashing that column — deterministic, no schema change, no migration. THE ONE CONSUMER THAT MUST MOVE IN THE SAME ACT: cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/an_inference_call_logs_that_it_started.py:104 counts `str(rec.get('pointer'))` against store canonicals today; unchanged, it would compare two vocabularies and report a disagreement that is an artifact of this ticket. PROSE IS THE LARGER HALF: `diagnostics.jsonl`/RECORD_NAME is spelled at 30 sites, few of them code — cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py:24 states the address as a promise and cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json states it inside falsifier clause (9); both are charter deltas owed in the same act, each poking cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh.
